title: careCycle price floor is the wedge
finding: careCycle entry pricing is ~$10,000/month for a 5-10 licensed agent operation (~$1,000-2,000 per agent per month), demo-and-custom-quote gated
impact: The only competitor with comparable Medicare depth does not compete for the 2-25 agent independent segment at all. The wedge is pricing before product.
action_implied: Publish pricing; lead GTM with accessible predictable cost and use plan depth as proof the price is not a downgrade

title: Feature 25 is not unique to us
finding: Coverage Voice markets "manage sub-accounts across multiple agencies", white-labelled under own brand and domain, live in 48 hours
impact: Sprint 1 scored feature 25 at +17.4 competitiveness on the basis that nobody offered it. Score should fall to roughly +6 to +8: a Q3 niche play, not a moat.
action_implied: Correct feature-scores.csv row 25 and re-derive quadrant; remove uniqueness claim from FMO collateral

title: SOA capture is an unroadmapped compliance gap
finding: Coverage Voice captures Scope of Appointment during the AI call alongside identity verification and eligibility confirmation before warm transfer
impact: SOA is a hard CMS requirement for a TPMO, not a convenience. It sits exactly between our benefit answer and our warm transfer - the moment we currently hand off.
action_implied: Add SOA capture to the pre-AEP roadmap alongside appointment scheduling; scope with the D5 compliance review

title: careCycle plan-context scope unknown
finding: Unclear whether careCycle's "member-aware call handling with plan/benefit context" covers pre-sale benefit Q&A or only post-enrolment member servicing
impact: Determines whether our plan-knowledge lead is wide or narrow - the core of the entire positioning
action_implied: Call careCycle as a prospect; ask whether a non-member caller can get a dental allowance answered

title: Agency branding parity unknown
finding: Unclear whether careCycle and Coverage Voice answer in the agency's name or their own
impact: Settles feature 16, scored -3.6 here but positive by both the source sheet and the Perplexity pass
action_implied: Call both as a prospect and listen to the greeting

title: Unverified capability claims about our own product
finding: A third-party research pass attributes provider lookup, consent capture and accessibility-oriented design for older adults to Health Plan Chat; none appear in the source feature sheet
impact: F15 provider network check is marked absent for us while MedicareCopilot and SunFire have it. Claiming it unverified would be a false capability claim against two competitors who demonstrably have it.
action_implied: Confirm against the product before any of the three appears in external material
